slot.brief: Solid floats at interface between two liquids with given fraction immersed; compare densities or find density of body

stem: Two solid blocks float fully submerged across the same interface of two immiscible liquids. Block $P$ has $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of its volume in the upper liquid, while block $Q$ has $\dfrac{1}{3}$ there. If $\rho_P:\rho_Q=3:4$, find the ratio of the upper to lower liquid densities.

verdicts.working: Buoyancy equilibrium gives \(\rho_P=(2\rho_u+\rho_l)/3\) and \(\rho_Q=(\rho_u+2\rho_l)/3\). Thus \((2\rho_u+\rho_l)/(\rho_u+2\rho_l)=3/4\), so \(\rho_u/\rho_l=2/5\).

working:
$$\rho_P=\dfrac{2\rho_u+\rho_l}{3},\qquad \rho_Q=\dfrac{\rho_u+2\rho_l}{3}$$
$$\dfrac{\rho_P}{\rho_Q}=\dfrac{3}{4}\Rightarrow 4(2\rho_u+\rho_l)=3(\rho_u+2\rho_l)$$
$$5\rho_u=2\rho_l\Rightarrow \rho_u:\rho_l=2:5$$

Independent check: Buoyancy equilibrium gives \(\rho_P=(2\rho_u+\rho_l)/3\) and \(\rho_Q=(\rho_u+2\rho_l)/3\). Thus \((2\rho_u+\rho_l)/(\rho_u+2\rho_l)=3/4\), so \(\rho_u/\rho_l=2/5\).
solution:
For floating equilibrium, each block’s density equals the volume-weighted average liquid density:
$$\rho_P=\frac{2\rho_u+\rho_l}{3},\qquad \rho_Q=\frac{\rho_u+2\rho_l}{3}$$
Using $\rho_P/\rho_Q=3/4$, we get $4(2\rho_u+\rho_l)=3(\rho_u+2\rho_l)$, hence $\rho_u:\rho_l=2:5$.
